Cancellation and downgrade copy promises the owner will 'choose which 3 people keep access' (app.js:1601-1604), but no member-selection step exists; analysis.md:193-194 acknowledges the policy is an unresolved assumption.
The billing tile's 'Change billing period' action opens a dialog headed 'Change plan' (app.js:549, 1082), a label/intent mismatch for a distinct task.
strengths: Plan, price, renewal date and member usage are all explicit and adjacent above the fold on desktop, with a clear 'Next payment' label and seat count.
Cancellation is separated after a rule and in its own page-nav entry, with plain consequences, an acknowledgement gate, a primary safe exit and reactivation.

Broad designed-state coverage: shaped loading skeleton, load failure with retry, empty invoices, past due, at-limit callout, scheduled-change notes with Undo, card errors and simulated provider failure.
Role handling keeps every read-only fact for members while replacing actions with local explanations rather than dead buttons.
Strong keyboard/focus craft (skip link, focus return, Escape blocked during work) and no color-contrast violation in the supplied axe run.

The claimed 71-check interaction suite is not supplied; test-output contains only structural/axe checks.

critical_defects: checks.json:31-42 and :70-81 report 6 serious color-contrast violations on both desktop and mobile; the node details are not included, so the affected elements cannot be confirmed from the packet.
Over-limit downgrade is a dead end: confirmation is disabled, the owner is told to remove members, but there is no member-management action or link (analysis.md:179; app.js:927-936).
Mobile prototype chrome consumes roughly 180px before the product UI and truncates the Data scenario value to 'Pro · approaching' (screenshots/mobile.png).
The summary's next-payment line reads '$29 on 1 December 2026' under the price without an explicit 'Next payment' label, unlike Candidate A.
strengths: One dominant summary makes plan, price, next-payment date, card and member usage scannable at a glance, with the usage consequence stated in plain language.
The Monthly/Annual control is explicitly a 'Price display' for comparison and the subscription stays unchanged until a separate reviewed action, avoiding a classic dark pattern.
Inline plan cards expose Free/Pro/Business limits and prices, while the review dialog shows the member-limit delta, prorated amount, effective date, next payment and payment method.
Cancellation review states access end date, no next payment, resulting Free limit, member consequences, invoice availability and undo, then requires an acknowledgement and offers a primary safe exit.
Honest payment states: failed payment remains unresolved after a card update, and every success message says no payment was processed.
Mobile invoice tables convert to labelled cards, and semantics such as aria-pressed, aria-busy and focus management are present.

comparison: Both are strong, complete prototypes that address the brief's owner and member needs. Candidate A is stronger on task and state coverage: it adds in-page navigation, an explicit 'Next payment' label, a select-to-review flow, scheduled-change Undo and cancellation gating, and its supplied axe run has no contrast failure. Candidate B is stronger visually and in plan comparison: one dominant summary, inline plan cards and a separate 'Price display' control that cannot silently change billing. Candidate A's mobile evidence is weakened by the prototype dock obscuring the usage count, while Candidate B has six contrast violations and a dead-end over-limit downgrade. Overall the pair is close, with A holding a small edge on the seven weighted dimensions.
limitations: This was one blinded judge pass, not a statistical test or proof of causation. Visual hierarchy was judged from only the supplied default owner screenshots (desktop 1280px and mobile 390px); no dialog, member-role, loading, error or success states are rendered as images, so those were assessed from code and the analyses. Both analyses cite a 1440px review, but the supplied screenshots and checks are 1280px wide, so the visual evidence is comparable but not the claimed 1440px render. The interaction counts in each analysis (36/36 and 71 checks) are not backed by logs; test-output/checks.json contains only structural and axe summaries, and axe does not list the offending nodes. No screen-reader testing, Firefox/Safari rendering, real payment-provider behavior or user research was available. Mobile compositions include prototype chrome that is not product UI but still affects the delivered screenshots.
